# Detecting hot spots with infrared thermography

A hot spot is a cell that dissipates the current of its neighbours because it
produces almost none of its own. Infrared thermography finds it from the ground:
the faulty cell reads ten to twenty kelvin above the module median under load.

## Bypass diodes and thermal patterns

A shaded substring activates its bypass diode, and the diode itself becomes the
warm element: that pattern is normal and moves with the shadow. A hot spot stays
in the same cell across passes and does not follow the sun, which is how the
inspection separates a defect from a transient shadow.

Fly the survey at midday with irradiance above six hundred watts per square
metre; below that threshold the thermal contrast is too small to trust.
